units.title: Politeness
units.intro: Grammar: reported (indirect) speech for statements, questions, requests and commands, and punctuation marks (colon, semi-colon, brackets, hyphen, apostrophe, quotation marks).

cards.title: Reported speech
rule: When the reporting verb is past (*said, asked, told*), the tense usually moves **one step back**: am/is → was; present simple → past simple; past simple → past perfect; will → would; can → could.
Pronouns and time words change: *now → then, today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, yesterday → the day before, here → there*.
**Questions:** *asked + if/whether* (yes/no) or *asked + wh-word*, with **statement word order** and no question mark. **Requests/commands:** *asked/told + object + (not) to + verb*.

examples.text: She said that she was tired.
He asked me where did I live.
examples.fix: He asked me where I lived.

examples.text: The teacher told us to sit down.

examples.fix: She told me not to go.

cards.pattern: said (that) + backshift  ·  asked if/wh- + statement order  ·  told + obj + to-inf

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: One of the most challenging obstacles facing high school graduates ________ the rising cost of higher education.

steps.text: The subject of the sentence is 'One' (singular) in the pattern $$\text{One of} + \text{Plural Noun} + \text{Singular Verb}$$.
The plural noun phrase 'the most challenging obstacles' is part of a prepositional phrase modifying the subject.
Students often match the verb to the plural noun 'obstacles' which is closest to the verb slot, leading them to choose 'are' (Option A).

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: The board of directors, despite having conflicting opinions on the new expansion policy, ________ finally agreed on the budget.

steps.text: The subject is 'The board' (singular collective noun).
The phrase 'of directors' and the parenthetical clause 'despite having conflicting opinions...' are intervening elements that do not change the subject's singular number.
Students are often distracted by the plural nouns 'directors' and 'opinions' and select the plural auxiliary 'have' (Option B).

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Neither the regional program coordinator nor the senior researchers ________ present at the emergency project meeting yesterday.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The compound subject is connected by the correlative conjunction 'Neither... nor'. The proximity rule applies, meaning the verb agrees with the closer subject, 'the senior researchers' (plural).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students may focus on 'the coordinator' (singular) and choose 'was' (Option A). The past time marker 'yesterday' eliminates present auxiliaries 'is' and 'are', leaving 'were' (Option B) as the correct choice.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
ምሉእ ሓሳብ ብ 'Neither... nor' ክእሰር ከሎ፡ እቲ ግሲ ምስቲ ናብኡ ዝቐረበ ባእታ ይሰማማዕ (Proximity Rule)። እቲ ዝቐረበ ባእታ 'the senior researchers' (ብዙሕ) ስለ ዝኾነን እቲ ግዜ ድማ 'yesterday' (ትማሊ) ስለ ዝኾነን፡ ቅኑዕ መልሲ 'were' (Option B) እዩ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The local police ________ currently searching the forest area for the prisoners who escaped from the regional jail.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
'Police' is a collective noun that is always plural in English and must be paired with plural verbs.

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Because 'police' does not end in '-s', students often assume it is singular and choose 'is' (Option A) or 'was' (Option C). The time marker 'currently' indicates present tense, which makes 'are' (Option B) correct.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
'Police' (ፖሊስ) ዝብል ስም ብቅርጹ ነጸላ ይመስል እምበር፡ ብሰዋስው ወግዒ ግን ወትሩ ብዙሕ ቁጽሪ (plural) እዩ። 'currently' (ኣብዚ እዋን) ዝብል ቃል ድማ ህልው እዋን ስለ ዝሕብር፡ ምስኡ ዝኸይድ ግሲ 'are' (Option B) እዩ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The teacher wanted to know how old I was. (Choose the correct direct speech)

options.A: “How old were you?” asked the teacher.
options.B: “How old am I?” asked the teacher.
options.C: “How old was I?” asked the teacher.
options.D: “How old are you?” asked the teacher.
options.E: “How old will you be?” asked the teacher.

cards.why: When converting reported speech back to direct speech, the past tense 'was' reverts to the present tense 'are', and the subject 'I' reverts to 'you'.

cards.title: Punctuation (2)
rule: **Quotation marks** enclose the exact words in direct speech: *“I’m sorry,” she said.* **Apostrophe** shows possession (*Meron’s bag*) or a missing letter (*don’t*). **Colon (:)** introduces a list or explanation. **Semi-colon (;)** joins two closely related sentences. **Hyphen (-)** joins compound words (*well-known*). **Brackets ( )** add extra information.

cards.title: Find and correct the error
cards.problem: Find and correct the error: "The boys bags are here."

steps.text: **Step 1: Recall the rule for this pattern.**
**Step 2: Test the sentence.** "The boys bags are here." breaks this rule.
**Step 3: Correct it.** "The boys’ bags are here."

cards.title: Memory tip
body: **One step back** in time, **statement order** for questions, **to-verb** for orders.

cards.title: Unit summary
body: In reported speech the tense moves back after a past reporting verb, pronouns and time words change, questions use if/whether or a wh-word with statement order, and requests or commands use asked/told + object + (not) to + verb.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which sentence is **correctly** capitalized and punctuated?

options.A: The secretary told me “the windows are not locked.”
options.B: The director told the students, “The exam starts at 08:30am.”
options.C: She said “The electric bill reading is 62:80 nakfa.”
options.D: The invigilator asked, “Do you all have admission cards?”
options.E: My father asked me, “where are you going”

cards.why: Option D follows all rules: a comma after the reporting verb, opening quotation marks, a capital letter for the start of the quote, and a question mark inside the quotation marks.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which of the following sentences is **correctly capitalized and punctuated**?

options.A: The policeman asked," Where do you come from,"
options.B: He shouted," didn't you hear the bell?"
options.C: Tom said, "i woke up feeling ill, so I didn't go to work."
options.D: She suggested, "why don't we go out for a meal tonight?

cards.why:
**Step 1:** In direct speech, there must be a comma after 'said'.
**Step 2:** The first letter inside the quotation marks must be a **Capital Letter**.
**Step 3:** The punctuation (period, question mark) must be **inside** the quotation marks. 
Choice E follows all rules: Tom said (comma), "I'm (Capital I) feeling ill." (Period inside).

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Abel said that they could change the date then even if it had been set. (Choose the correct direct speech form)

options.A: “Although the date has been set” , said Abel and added, “ We can change it now.”
options.B: “Although the date has been set,” said Abel and added, “We can change it now.”
options.C: “Although the date has been set,”said Abel and added, “we can change it now.”
options.D: “Although the date has been set,” said Abel, and added, “ We can change it now.”
options.E: All are possible direct speech forms

cards.why: Choice B follows standard English punctuation rules: the comma is inside the quotation marks, there is a space after the comma, and the second quote starts with a capital letter.
